heroHeadline: Zero Day: Mohamud Mandate Expires — Opposition Declares Him Illegitimate, National Salvation Conference Announced; Piracy Global Spotlight as CNN Reports Day 20/19/13 Crisis; MT Eureka Ransom Raised to $10M
heroSubtitle: Somalia's constitutional crisis reached its defining moment on May 15, 2026, as President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's four-year term under the 2012 provisional constitution formally expired. The opposition Somali Future Council — led by Puntland's Deni and Jubbaland's Madobe — declared Mohamud's presidency illegitimate and announced a National Salvation Conference to form a rival transitional authority, while government-opposition talks continued even on deadline day itself in a final last-chance session with no deal yet announced. The May 16 mass protest in Mogadishu remained locked in. Simultaneously, Somalia's three-vessel piracy crisis entered international headlines: CNN, Cyprus Mail, and Cyprus Shipping News all published major May 15 analyses linking the resurgence to the Iran War diverting naval patrols away from the Horn of Africa. Honour 25 reached Day 20 (17 crew; $7M pirate demand deadlocked), Sward Day 19 (15 crew), and MT Eureka Day 13 (12 crew) — with pirates raising the Eureka ransom demand to $10M, citing negotiation frustration. Total simultaneous hostages: 44. Al-Shabaab held Adan Yabal for Day 26, exploiting the governance vacuum as Somalia's political class remained consumed by the constitutional impasse. AFRICOM's confirmed strike count held at 63+ as of May 7; no new AFRICOM press releases issued since PR #36471.
footerNote: Data sourced from ACLED, OCHA, UNSOM, WFP, AFRICOM, EU EPF, EU NAVFOR, Combined Maritime Forces, UN Monitoring Group, World Bank, IPC, and major international outlets. Casualty figures contested where noted.
